questions: What should be plotted on the histogram when the DataFrame is empty? The clarification says 'empty plot (Axes object with no data)', but does that mean no histogram bars at all, or an empty histogram (zero-height bars)?

Should the histogram use density=True (probability density) or density=False (raw frequency counts)? The reference solution uses density=True, but the prompt's y-axis label is 'Frequency', which might imply counts.
When fitting the normal distribution, should it be fitted to all data (including non-duplicates) or only to duplicate values? The prompt says 'fitted to the data' but doesn't specify which data.
What should happen if the data has only one unique value (constant)? The reference solution sets mu, std to None, but the prompt doesn't specify whether to plot the normal curve in that case.

For the duplicate counter, should it count all occurrences of each duplicate value, or only the extra occurrences beyond the first? The prompt says 'count of each duplicate value', but 'duplicate' could mean repeated (all) or extra copies.
Should the normal distribution curve be plotted even if the fit parameters are invalid (e.g., std=0)? The reference avoids it when mu/std are None, but the prompt doesn't define 'if applicable'.
What is the expected behavior if the 'value' column contains NaN values? Should they be ignored, cause an error, or be treated as a value?
Should the histogram bins be computed based on the range of all data or only duplicate values? The prompt mentions 'all values in the 'value' column' for the histogram, but not for bin edges.
